reports.title: PicPay’s third-quarter 2026 results, excluding any contribution from Kev, met or exceeded all nine guidance metrics we gave in August, and we did it while becoming more efficient, not less.

lines: We expect the implementation of the new policy in the fourth quarter of 2026 to result in a one-time net income impact of approximately R$ 325 million on our quarterly earnings, with no cash impact.

Looking ahead, even after absorbing the impact of the write-off policy change in the fourth quarter, we expect to close the year with a total capital ratio between 13% and 13.5%, and a common equity tier 1 ratio between 11% and 11.5%.

Under the current policy, full-year adjusted net income is expected to be approximately R$1,058 million, compared with approximately R$733 million under the new policy, which includes a one-time charge of approximately R$325 million recognized in 4Q26.
Beyond 2026, we expect NPLs over 90 days to stabilize at approximately 9% in 2Q27.

desk.headline: Revenue up 73% to R$4.73bn (ex-Kev), above estimates, and adjusted profit up 157%; Q4 guided to R$334m adjusted profit before a R$325m one-off write-off charge
results: Excluding newly bought insurer Kev, revenue rose 73% to R$4.73bn and adjusted net income jumped 157% to R$271.2m; PicPay met or beat all nine of its Q3 guidance targets.
The loan book grew 88% to R$35.0bn, led by private payroll loans (R$9.0bn, up more than six-fold).
Bad loans rose as the young book ages: loans over 90 days late reached 10.7% (9.8% in Q2), though quarterly cost of risk eased to 3.8%.
Costs grew slower than revenue, cutting the efficiency ratio to 42.4% from 53.8%; clients reached 72.0m accounts and 46.4m active users.
Including Kev (August–September) and intercompany eliminations, consolidated net income was R$210.2m; the Kev deal cut the capital ratio by 1.8 points to 15.0%.

guidance.summary: For Q4 (ex-Kev) PicPay expects a R$37.1bn loan book, about R$4.2bn managerial revenue and about R$334m adjusted profit under its current accounting. From Q4 it will write off unsecured personal loans after 120 days instead of 360, a one-off R$325m hit to profit with no cash impact, cutting full-year adjusted profit to about R$733m from about R$1,058m.

points: Management says credit is the main growth engine but is being grown with discipline, favouring payroll loans and cards for clients with 12+ months on the app.
It blames rising delinquency on the book maturing and a debt-renegotiation programme, not weaker underwriting; NPL 90+ seen near 9% by Q2 2027.
The faster write-off rule is described as a one-time accounting change that leaves risk appetite and growth plans unchanged.
Kev insurance is pitched as a new growth stream; an accounting timing effect from intercompany commissions should fade over coming quarters.
AI-driven efficiency is highlighted: revenue per client rose 58% while cost to serve rose 20%.
call.source: Management letter and outlook in the earnings release (Exhibit 99.1); no independent call coverage found
